subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Leah Martin <leah.martin@finsecure.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@finsecure.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Leah / Carlos,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear framing on FinSecure's requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary constraint: customer data (PII + transaction logs) cannot be accessible to any third party and must remain under FinSecure control.
- Desired deployment options under consideration: Private VPC (preferred if we can meet "data never leaves VPC" requirement) vs Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPU pools managed by Redwood, but runs in Redwood-managed network).
- Key compliance asks: BYOK/KMS integration, audit logging (retention 2+ years), SAML/SSO for admin access, and evidence for SOC 2 controls.

Clarifying questions we have to validate which path is right for you:
1) When you say "data cannot leave our VPC," do you require literal in-VPC compute (i.e., our on-prem or VPC connectors where no egress to Redwood-managed network occurs), or would a private peering/VPC-to-VPC model (Redwood Private) where logs + KV caches are encrypted and no data is stored in shared buckets be acceptable?
2) Will FinSecure require a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) model for model inputs/outputs or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable for an initial POC?
3) Any constraints around latency or throughput that would push toward on-prem local inference vs a VPC deployment?

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in our Solutions Engineer (Avery) and Security lead (Neha) for a technical deep-dive to walk through network architecture options (Private VPC peering vs Dedicated with strict tenancy controls).
- I'll share our deployment matrix + security FAQ and our SOC 2 evidence link prior to the call.

Can you confirm availability for a 60-minute technical call next week? Suggested slots: Tue 3/31 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 4/1 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — happy to adapt depending on your procurement timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Leah Martin <leah.martin@finsecure.com>

Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- "Cannot leave our VPC" means that customer-identifiable data (including derived embeddings and any request/response logs) must not be stored on a multi-tenant Redwood-managed storage outside our control. We need either:
  a) A Private VPC deployment where compute is in our AWS account (Redwood-managed control plane only), or
  b) An on-prem option (air-gapped) if Private VPC cannot guarantee zero-exfiltration.

- BYOK: We prefer BYOK for all production workloads. For a short POC (2–4 weeks) we can accept Redwood-managed KMS if you can guarantee key isolation and automatic key deletion after the POC.

- Audit & logging: We need admin and API access logs with a 2-year retention and immutable storage (or exportable to our logging bucket).

- Compliance: FinSecure is SOC 2 type II and pursuing FedRAMP Lite for certain products — we will need to review your evidence. Can you send SOC 2 report and any relevant architecture docs?

I'll attach our security questionnaire so your security team can pre-fill answers: FinSecure-Security-Questionnaire.pdf (attached).

Carlos and I are available for the technical deep-dive on Tue 3/31 10:00 PT — that works for us.

Leah
Leah Martin
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure
leah.martin@finsecure.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Thanks Leah — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Avery (Solutions Engineer) and Neha (Security) to prepare the technical deep-dive and pre-fill your questionnaire where we can. 

High-level differences (so you have the framing ahead of the call):

Option A — Redwood Private (VPC deployment):
- Compute runs in your AWS account (we deploy an agent/AMI into a customer-managed VPC).
- Control plane for orchestration remains in Redwood, but no customer data is written to Redwood-managed shared storage.
- Supports BYOK (integration with customer KMS) and customer-managed log retention (you can pipe logs to your S3).
- Best fit when "data cannot leave VPC" is a hard requirement and you want minimum network egress risk.

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Dedicated, single-tenant GPU pools managed by Redwood in our infrastructure.
- Strong tenancy isolation and no multi-tenant process access, but networking is Redwood-managed (private subnets in our cloud).
- May be acceptable if FinSecure can accept outbound peering to a dedicated, isolated network and if BYOK + strict logging guarantees are provided — we will detail these controls on the call.

Questions for your security/infra team to help us finalize recommendation: 
1) Do you require that inference compute run inside your own account/VPC (yes/no)?
2) For PII/Risk classification: is encryption-at-rest with BYOK mandatory from day one, or can it be gated to production?
3) Are there specific compliance artifacts (FedRAMP boundary diagrams, encryption standards) we should prepare in advance?

Attachments I shared: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf and our Private VPC security FAQ (redwood-private-vpc-security-faq.pdf). We'll also send SOC 2 redaction-ready copies through a secure link prior to the call.

Confirmed: Tue 3/31 10:00–11:00 PT works — joining call with Avery and Neha.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-security-faq.pdf

Leah / team — quick technical note ahead of tomorrow's deep-dive (attached diagram + short checklist).

Key checklist items we'll cover on the call:
- Network model options: VPC peering vs Private Link vs deployed agent in-customer VPC (tradeoffs on egress controls).
- KMS integration details: customer CMK support, key rotation, and how we ensure key material never leaves your account.
- Logging and retention: options to stream API request/response logs to your S3/CloudWatch; we support immutable WORM S3 buckets and export to your SIEM.
- Data lifecycle: how transient artifacts (KV caches, model context) are kept ephemeral and can be scrubbed after inference; options for no persistent storage.

I attached an architecture diagram showing the Private VPC deployment pattern and a short checklist we can use to capture your answers in the call. If you can confirm which of the following apply, we can bring concrete designs: 
- You require compute inside your AWS account (yes/no)
- BYOK required (yes/no)
- Exportable immutable logs required (yes/no)

Suggested times (re-affirming): Tue 3/31 10:00–11:00 PT — I will drop an invite.
